assessment.intent: Clear. The article teaches small business owners to compare web design quotes by shared brief, worksheet, scope, technical fit and support rather than price alone.
assessment.specificity: Good. It names concrete categories to compare, includes a useful worksheet table, gives grounded examples like service-area pages, a 40-page blog migration and a brochure site versus an e-commerce build.
assessment.evidence: Appropriate and restrained. It links to Google, W3C and Webflow where relevant without inventing results or overclaiming. Hypothetical examples are clearly framed as examples.
assessment.voice: Close to Michael. It is practical, direct and Canadian in tone, with connected conversational sentences and a clear owner-focused tradeoff.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. The worksheet and quote-comparison guidance give business owners a concrete tool, not just a checklist of ideas.
